panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of left palm showing brown pigmented macule in 9-year-old boy from tinea nigra case report titled 'The first report of tinea nigra from Iran'; matches textbook palmar brown-black macule.
panels.attribution_text: Kelarestaghi et al. The first report of tinea nigra from Iran.. New microbes and new infections 2022. doi:10.1016/j.nmni.2022.101032. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Pigmented macule on the left palm.
in_text_mentions: A 9-year-old rural boy from Amol, Mazandaran, northern Iran presented with a 2-year history of a lowly growing asymptomatic hyperpigmented macules on his left palm. He denied pruritus or pain and no other parts of the body were affected. He had no relevant history of trauma or underlying disorders. On physical examination, a brown four-centimeter macula, with irregular pigmentation and shape; it had defined edges, without scales or symptoms of inflammation (Fig. 1). There was no history of a similar condition in the family.Fig. 1Pigmented macule on the left palm.Fig. 1

panels.rationale: Single-image KOH mount from patient's lesional skin scrapings in tinea nigra case report with in-text description of branching septate pigmented hyphae matching vocabulary finding.
panels.attribution_text: Kelarestaghi et al. The first report of tinea nigra from Iran.. New microbes and new infections 2022. doi:10.1016/j.nmni.2022.101032. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
in_text_mentions: The patient's lesional skin scrapings were taken. For direct microscopic examination, the specimen was prepared in KOH 10% solution and observed under a microscope. The skin scrapings revealed numerous branching and septate hyphae of various diameters when examined under the microscope. The hyphae's apical part was hyaline, with parallel walls and regular septation. The oldest sections have a brownish color, a wavy cell wall, and irregularly distributed septa. (Fig. 2).Fig. 2KOH preparation in microscopic observation.Fig. 2

panels.rationale: Single microscopy image from tinea nigra case report showing dematiaceous septate hyphae attributed to Hortaea werneckii, matching KOH mount finding vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Lima Dantas et al. Entodermoscopy in the Diagnosis of Tinea Nigra: Two Case Reports.. Dermatology practical & conceptual 2020. doi:10.5826/dpc.1003a65. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Mycological examination: dematiaceous septate and branched hyphae.
in_text_mentions: Both patients were from Porto Alegre, Brazil, and had the lesions for approximately 8 months. Mycological examination showed dematiaceous septate hyphae (Figure 3), and Hortaea werneckii was identified in culture. Both patients were treated with fenticonazole cream for 30 days and showed clinical improvement.

A: Gross clinical photo of brown irregular patch in toe web in article titled Interdigital Tinea Nigra; matches foot pigmented macule of tinea nigra in variant interdigital location.
